title: Flag-Guarded Dead Codepath Graveyard (CI Flag-Guard Leftovers)
pattern: A runtime conditional branch (`if/else`) where one of the paths (typically the old codepath) is dead wood but remains checked into version control long after the flag has been permanently configured to the alternative.
why_bad: Accumulated complexity and "haunted graveyards". Keeping dead branches inside binaries raises cyclomatic complexity, increases binary footprints, degrades compiler optimization potential, and prevents the cleanup of obsolete dependencies and data schemas.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. A branch statement controlled by a runtime feature flag.
2. The associated feature flag is retired (always `true` or `false` in configuration), or the code path has been under-utilized/unexecuted in production for an extended period according to telemetry.
strength: Contextual` (Requires configuration or runtime trace telemetry to verify flag retirement)
source:
- Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020) [370]
- Kent Beck, *Tidy First?* (2023) [71, 72]
